title: fix: end visitor access when its grant ends
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A visitor admitted while an invitation is active can retain an open Gateway connection or accepted run after that invitation expires or is revoked. Losing the original email identity or the Visitor Access plugin can also leave previously captured authority usable.

## User Impact

Expiry, revocation and original-identity loss end the captured visitor authority across WebSocket, HTTP, direct tool and OpenAI-compatible requests, including active and queued Gateway runs. Cancellation preserves saved work and joins accepted terminal and partial-transcript writes. Independent staff and Gateway-owner authority remains usable.

Operators can bind the existing guest role to `accessPolicyPlugin: "visitor-access"`. The role then requires that policy even when its manifest is absent or invalid, loading fails, it is disabled, or startup is incomplete. Unbound staff roles and the Gateway owner retain their independent access. Guest admission on older code without this binding is unsupported; recovery keeps the binding and restricted role intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requests and accepted runs retain the invitation under which they were admitted. Renewing an active invitation keeps its generation; inviting someone again after expiry creates a new generation and cannot revive ended work. Exact run identity and lifecycle generation keep cancellation from affecting replacement or independent work. A captured invitation also ends when its original email alias moves to another profile; restoring the alias cannot revive it.

The durable invitation becomes active only after confirmed provider membership. Failed or uncertain provider writes keep an inactive cleanup record or preserve the previous deadline. Legacy records require positive membership confirmation before use, while qualified grants retain their local expiry across restart. Native cancellation signals survive plugin retirement and garbage collection while callbacks remain bound to their original instance. Configuration help, SDK documentation and the Visitor Access README describe these contracts.

## Evidence

The real Gateway revoke flow passed using the registered `visitor_invite` and `visitor_revoke` tools, native state, a restricted Guest and independent staff, and a loopback Responses provider. It observed both an active Guest request and an actual scheduler-queued request, then verified both tasks cancelled, the active provider response closed, the queued request made no provider call, and a new Guest connection was forbidden. Staff completed after its recorded Visitor grant was revoked; saved Guest input, creator and sandbox requirement were preserved.

That bounded integration used source `67699e4` plus the declared consumer scope fixture for an explicit-session, no-delivery `agent` request with `operator.sessions.write`. It does not claim complete Guest session creation, UI, model-tool, delivery or descendant-process behavior. Expiry, alias loss and restoration, absent/broken required plugins, native SQLite commit-time refusal, same-period renewal and new-period separation have separate owner-level coverage.

The cancellation correction has causal red/green proof and passed 40 affected cases, typed lint, production types and all 24 selected core test graphs. Earlier qualified batches cover 509 Gateway cases, 15 Visitor lifecycle cases, 11 loader cases, 86 inline-action cases, 99 HTTP/context/policy cases and native Node 24 retirement/GC. The original native retirement crash and alias-restoration regression fail on the previous owners and pass with the fixes.

The invitation, run-source and scope prerequisites are effective on `main` (#153987, #153989, #154392). The main integration at `09d10c0` passed 174 selected cases covering the real Gateway retained-state fixture, native writer guards, plugin retirement/GC, HTTP/WebSocket identity, cookie lifetime, config validation and Visitor lifecycle. Typed fixture lint and production types pass. The retained-state case verifies that positive provider qualification gives a legacy grant its generation without changing its original metadata or deadline; renewal retains that generation, an unassigned Guest without a grant is denied, and staff/owner profiles remain unchanged.

The native fixture checks captured authority observations after settlement, outside the admission callback's exception handler. Both revocation timings therefore assert immediate execution-authority loss while independently checking refusal before commit and preservation after commit. The corrected five-case order passes without its former swallowed-assertion warning.

The final-head refresh on `82a1b0d0`, after the generated-fingerprint replay onto `1c573c48`, passes 14 native Gateway/writer cases, 6 focused HTTP/WebSocket grant and alias-retirement cases, 124 runtime-build selection cases, and core production types. It uses the rebuilt runtime and retains the warning observer; no admission-cleanup warning remains. Hosted CI, including production and test types, documentation and architecture checks, and Security Review passed. Completed exact-head review artifacts are Platinum with no code or security findings.


The published `openclaw@2026.9.5` updater also passed a Visitor-specific retained-state cell against the built `82a1b0d0` candidate. The real installed `openclaw update --no-restart --yes --tag ... --json` preserved the legacy no-ID grant, profiles, aliases, role and provider configuration; both native schema-17 snapshot preflights passed. Candidate-only Guest scopes and the required policy binding were adopted after the update. The actual Gateway denied Guest admission while Visitor was disabled, then positively qualified the retained grant through the registered Visitor service and tool, admitted the granted Guest and denied the ungranted Guest, while staff and shared-owner access remained usable. Qualification preserved the original grant metadata and deadline, and the loopback membership provider observed only reads.

That cell retained the unmodified core package and separately inventoried the same build's private Visitor payload, which is excluded from normal npm packages. The maintained metadata-only future-version fixture forced a genuine update; the private bundled supplement preserved native installed SDK/runtime resolution. This is forward adoption from released-valid configuration, with no older Gateway serving Guest and no downgrade, live Cloudflare, managed-service replacement or full Guest-delivery claim. This contribution does not activate a live Gateway.
